findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being earlier in the chain
findings.body: The explicit pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID log params were removed. The log line now only carries them if `FromContext(ctx)` finds contextual attributes set by `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`. That coupling is implicit: `NewLoggerMiddleware` can be wired without the contextual middleware, for example by enterprise or other callers of `CreateMiddlewares`, or after a reorder. In that case the "Plugin Request Completed" / grafana-data-egress log lines lose the plugin and datasource identity, which makes them much less useful. Nothing documents or enforces the ordering. The old doc comment saying the instrumentation middleware must be at the top was deleted and not replaced on the new middleware.

findings.title: No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware or the refactored LoggerMiddleware
findings.body: Logic that used to be inside the instrumentation middleware (building contextual attributes from the plugin context, including the optional datasource and user fields) now lives in a new middleware with no test. The `LoggerMiddleware` change to `FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` is also untested. The only test touched is the renamed metrics test. A regression where the contextual attributes are not attached, or are attached to the wrong endpoint, would go unnoticed. Add tests that run a request through the contextual middleware and assert on the attributes the logger sees.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so recorded calls are lost
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a new instance, instead of the receiver. `LoggerMiddleware` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. Any test that injects a `TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware` and asserts on `InfoLogs` will see zero calls, because the call is recorded on a throwaway instance. Return `f` (or a logger sharing the same `Logs` state) so the fake is usable for asserting on logs.

findings.title: FromContext silently drops context when the type assertion fails
findings.body: If `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` does not return a `*log.ConcreteLogger`, the code falls back to `d.New()`. That is the original logger without any context attributes, and nothing is logged about the fallback. The caller then emits log lines without the contextual plugin and request attributes. The path is silent and untested, so a change in the infra logger's return type would quietly degrade logging.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported plugins Logger interface is a breaking change
findings.body: `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` was added to the public `log.Logger` interface. Any other implementation of this interface, such as fakes, wrappers or enterprise or out-of-tree code, no longer compiles. This is reasonable for the feature, but it is a contract break, and the PR description does not call it out. The same file also converts `interface{}` to `any` across unrelated signatures, which adds diff noise.

findings.title: Test function and leftovers still use the old Instrumentation naming
findings.body: The file was renamed to `metrics_middleware_test.go`, but the test is still named `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. Leftovers of the old name remain elsewhere: the `imw` variable in `NewMetricsMiddleware`, the `instrumentContext` helper that now lives in the contextual logger middleware, and the `plugin.instrumentation` logger name in `pluginsintegration.go`. This contradicts the stated goal of naming consistency and makes `go test -run TestMetricsMiddleware` miss the test.
